newsitem.title: UK: UK's Halifax makes debut at 774-1/2p.
newsitem.headline: UK's Halifax makes debut at 774-1/2p.

text.p: Britain biggest mortgage lender, Halifax Building Society Plc started its first day's trade on the London Stock Exchange on Monday at 774-1/2p, valuing the group at around 19.4 billion stg.
At the current share price, the Halifax is ranked as the 16th largest listed UK company in terms of market capitalisation, according to data from Reuters Securities 3000.
Some 7.6 million Halifax savers and borrowers have become shareholders in the flotation. Until today Halifax, like Britain's other building societies, has been owned by its members.
Last February, they voted in favour of a proposal to convert to a public limited company and float on the stock exchange.

The Halifax said around 570 million shares or 23 percent of its issued share capital had been auctioned on Friday to institutional investors at an average price of 732.5 pence per share. Around 600 million shares had traded by 0740 GMT.
Analysts say Halifax will be a leader in the financial services industry, with a profitable existing franchise and extensive capital reserves -- estimated at more than three billion pounds.
